name: Which Street Looks More Walkable? (Anyang and Seoul)
description:
Method replication: participants compare 30 pairs of street views from Anyang and Yeongdeungpo (Seoul) and click the one they perceive as more walkable, or Equal; the city is named under each image. The images are not the paper's stimuli (67 Google Street View views, 2015–2018, each facing front, back, left or right at random, fetched for this template).
Original study: Choi & Kang (2025), "Modeling and explaining perceived walkability in urban environments using street view images and explainable AI", Spatial Information Research 33, 57. Street views in four directions were collected every 30 m in Anyang and Yeongdeungpo; 20,886 images stratified by road type and land use formed the survey set. On a web platform, 65 evaluators (25 in their 20s, 20 in their 30s–40s, 20 aged 50 or older) picked the more walkable image in sets of 50 pairs, each set with five control pairs; 174,118 valid choices (excluding "equal") trained an RSS-Swin model, and AutoML with SHAP explained the scores with segmented street elements.
Differences from the original study: (1) 67 new Google Street View images instead of the paper's 20,886, not stratified by road type and land use; (2) 30 pairs per participant without control pairs, instead of sets of 50 with five control pairs; (3) open to anyone, with questions on age group and gender.
author: Choi & Kang
